decisions.decision: The plan stores deadlines as optional fields in the version 1 data file so unmodified 1.4.0 can start and list every ticket, accepting that a subsequent 1.4.0 save can erase those deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected rollback to preserve the exact deadlines through writes on 1.4.0 and a later re-upgrade, including for tickets whose priority has since changed.

decisions.decision: Operators must stop the service that writes the file, run a separate offline backfill against that file, and then start the service with due times enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the service to backfill in the background while continuing to answer requests, with activation deferred until the file was ready.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:13 (summary); record/06-plan.md:78–101 (migration, switchover and concurrency); record/08-step-plan-W1.md:149 (command rehearsal)

decisions.decision: If due times are enabled and a saved ticket has no deadline, the service exits before listening and reports a missing-deadline error.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the service to remain available in its legacy mode and warn operators until they complete the migration.

decisions.decision: For older tickets the backfill uses the priority stored on each ticket at migration time, even if it has changed since creation.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected each original promise to use the ticket's priority at creation, recovered from the audit history.

decisions.decision: The backfill uses the response-hour settings in effect when the migration command runs for tickets still missing deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected existing tickets to use the four original response-time values, with overrides applying only to newly created tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–6,11–12 (R-1 and R-4); record/09-test-spec-W1.md:25–29 (backfill configuration and retry in TC-2)

decisions.decision: The plan assigns and stores deadlines when the new release creates tickets with the feature off, using the flag to gate their visibility and overdue filtering.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected tickets created while the switch was off to get their first deadlines during the pre-activation backfill.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–10 (R-1 through R-3); record/06-plan.md:59–75 (API and state decisions)

decisions.decision: Response times use continuous elapsed hours from creation, so deadlines can fall outside support hours.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant hours on the help desk's working calendar, with the clock paused overnight, on weekends or on holidays.

decisions.decision: Operators set response times through four optional, validated per-priority environment overrides read at process startup.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted help-desk leads to change the hours for future tickets through a live setting without asking operators to restart the service.

decisions.decision: Backfill adds all missing deadlines in one atomic save and leaves a fully migrated file alone on retry, even if the configured hours have changed.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a resumable migration that commits deadlines in batches and can leave a partly migrated file while activation is blocked.

decisions.decision: Delivery consists of local changes, an operator procedure, and a local rehearsal, with production rollout left to the operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the work to include running the migration and activating the feature in production.

decisions.decision: When overdue filtering is enabled, a ticket must be overdue and match either the requested status or the requested priority when both existing filters are supplied, following the running service's behavior.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the overdue list to require both supplied filters, as the existing API documentation says.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:13 (code and tests take precedence); repo/docs/shiploop/architecture.md:17–18 (AD-2); repo/docs/api.md:67–77 (documented filter behavior)

decisions.decision: Enabled ticket responses expose `due` as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted an epoch value or an explicit local-offset timestamp for API clients.

decisions.decision: The enabled API includes `due` wherever it returns a ticket, including responses to creation, edits and lifecycle transitions as well as reads.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant to expose deadlines in ticket reads and listings while keeping write-response payloads compatible with existing clients.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:7–8 (R-2); repo/docs/shiploop/architecture.md:8–10 (HTTP creation, patch and visibility checks); repo/src/app.js:22–39 (ticket response routes)

decisions.decision: The overdue predicate is applied before cursor pagination, so the page size and continuation reflect the overdue matches.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected overdue filtering within each existing unfiltered page so clients could reuse the same page boundaries.

decisions.decision: The plan leaves the ticket audit history intact, so the offline backfill does not create an audit entry for each deadline it sets.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected agents to see a deadline assignment and its migration time in each ticket's history.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:11–12 (backfill preserves other logical state); record/06-plan.md:65–69 (audit and outbox)

decisions.decision: The plan leaves requester notifications as they are when ticket deadlines are introduced.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the acknowledgment for newly opened tickets to tell the recipient the promised response deadline.
decisions.where: record/06-plan.md:65–69 (audit and outbox preserved); repo/src/templates.js:8–12 (existing acknowledgment)

decisions.decision: The human-readable CLI list and show views display the deadline only when `DUE_TIMES=on` is set for the CLI invocation.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the release switch to govern the HTTP service while letting operators inspect stored deadlines in the CLI before activation.

decisions.decision: The raw CLI listing keeps exactly its existing four columns, leaving the weekly report without deadline data.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a deadline in machine-readable output, for example through a new opt-in format that preserves existing report inputs.

decisions.decision: Only the exact `overdue=true` value activates the new HTTP filter.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a full Boolean filter that also supports `overdue=false` to select tickets that are not overdue.

decisions.decision: An active ticket becomes overdue only once the request clock is strictly later than its deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a ticket counted as overdue at the exact deadline.
